These appeals are arising out of common judgment and award dated 04.11.2017 passed in M.V.C. No.18/2016 on the file of Prl. Senior Civil Judge and AMACT,
Ranebennur ("the Tribunal" for short), they are heard together and disposed off by this common judgment.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as they are referred to in the claim petitions before the Tribunal.

3. M.F.A. No.102061/2018 is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, whereas, M.F.A. No.100941/2018 is filed by the Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation ("Corporation" for short), insurer of the offending vehicle seeking reduction of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and also challenging the liability fastened on the Corporation.

The brief facts of the claimants case before the Tribunal is as under:

On 19.06.2015 at about 07:30 p.m., the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider along with his friends in motorcycle bearing registered No.KA-27/H-6513 on P.B.Road, Davanagere, at that time, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing registered No.KA-17/F-1693 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased sustained fatal injuries to all over the body.

Immediately he was shifted to Shymanuru Shivashankarappa Institute of Medical Sciences Research Centre Hospital, Davangere,
wherein the injured succumbed to the accidental injuries.

Aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the claimants preferred M.F.A.
No.102061/2018 seeking enhancement and the  -6-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7858  MFA No. 102061 of 2018  MFA No.100941/2018 Corporation preferred M.F.A. No.100941/2018 seeking reduction of compensation and also challenging the liability.

Hence, he prayed to allow the appeal.
7. Learned counsel for Corporation contended that two vehicles are involved in the accident.

The rider of the motorcycle who in order to take right turn to go to his village side crossed the road, without any signal or indication, rode the motorcycle which caused accident and hence, the Tribunal ought to have held that due to entire  -7-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7858  MFA No. 102061 of 2018  MFA No.100941/2018 negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, the accident in question was occurred.
It is further contended that the in all persons were traveling in motorcycle which is prohibited under Section 128 of M.V. Act.
It is also contended that the Tribunal has not justified in calculating the income of deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month in the absence of any material on record.

The Tribunal considering the oral and documentary evidence on record Sri. Nagappa S/O. Muniyappa Lamani vs The Managing Director on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60862715/

In view of the submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties, the following points that would arise for consideration by this Court are as follows:
 i. "Whether the Corporation proved that the  rider of motorcycle also contributed negligence  -8-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7858  MFA No. 102061 of 2018  MFA No.100941/2018  and hence, Corporation is not liable to pay entire  compensation?"
 ii.

"Whether the quantum of compensation  awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or  does it call for enhancement?"

From the perusal of the pleadings, documents,
evidence on record, it appears that, PW.1 in their evidence clearly stated that the alleged incident took place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus vehicle bearing registered No.KA-17/F-1693 and the accident took place while the diver over taking motorcycle,
he dashed to the motorcycle of deceased.

From the perusal of Column No.17 of charge sheet, it clearly establishes that on 19.06.2015 at about 7.30 P.M., the rider of motorcycle bearing registered  -9-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7858  MFA No. 102061 of 2018  MFA No.100941/2018 No.KA-27/H-6513 was proceeding on P.B.road Davanagere, at that time, the driver of KSRTC bus came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle.
Hence, the accident in question was caused to the sole negligent act of driver of the KSRTC bus.

12 . However, the Tribunal without appreciating the evidence on record in a proper perspective manner saddled liability on the rider of motorcycle which is in contravention of the contents of charge sheet.

Admittedly,
the Corporation has not challenged the contents of charge sheet.
Therefore, the Corporation is alone liable to pay compensation.

13. After hearing the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perusing the judgment and award of the Tribunal, I am of the view that the compensation awarded Sri. Nagappa S/O. Muniyappa Lamani vs The Managing Director on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60862715/

sentences.text: The claimants in order to prove their case examined Sri.Nagappa S/o Muniyappa Lamani-father of deceased as PW.1

and got exhibited documents namely Exs.P.1 to P.44.
 15.

The claimants have stated that prior to death of deceased, he was aged about 19 years, hale and healthy person and the deceased was a bachelor and was doing Goundi Mestri work and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month as on the date of accident and was contributing the same to his family.
Claimants have not produced any proof of income.

Under such circumstances, the Tribunal considered notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/-
per month, however, the observations made by the Tribunal in this regard is not correct.

Considering the age of the deceased as 19 years, year of the accident as 2015,
his notional income is re
- assessed at Rs.8,000/- per month instead of Rs.7,000/- per month, as arrived at by the Tribunal.

- 11 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7858  MFA No. 102061 of 2018  MFA No.100941/2018 Sri. Nagappa S/O. Muniyappa Lamani vs The Managing Director on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60862715/

Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the accident is of the year 2015.
The deceased died bachelor, who was aged about 19 years at the time of accident.
Hence, the future prospects should be taken at 40%.
The claimants have not furnished any documents to prove the income of the deceased.

Hence, the notional income at Rs.8,000/- per month is taken into consideration, which comes to Rs.3,200/- (Rs.8,000/- +
40% = Rs.11,200).
The multiplier applicable to his age group is '18'.
Since, the deceased was bachelor at the time of accident, 50% income has to be deducted from his personal income.

Therefore, the 'loss of dependency'
works out to Rs.12,09,600/- (Rs.8,000/- + 40% X 12 X 18 - 50%) against Rs.11,85,526/-, as awarded by the Tribunal.

17. The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards 'transportation of dead body',
Rs.25,000/- towards 'funeral expenses', Rs.10,000/-
towards 'loss of estate', Rs.79,726/- towards 'medical  - 12 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7858  MFA No. 102061 of 2018  MFA No.100941/2018 expenses' and Rs.1,25,000/- towards 'love and affection,
which are not reasonable one.
 18.

In view of the decision cited supra, only parents are entitled for loss of consortium and earning brothers (petitioner Nos.3 to 5) are not entitled for loss of consortium.
Hence, claimant Nos.1 and 2 alone are entitled for sum of Rs.40,000/- each under the head 'loss of consortium'.

19. In view of ratio laid down in case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and Magma (supra), a sum of Rs.15,000/-
